# Outline — what the paper says and what carries it (revision 6: first results from `analysis`, verdicts per claim)

Source: `idea-repo` Brief revision 6 (the idea, the predictions P1–P5, the study design and cell budget), the objective (`story-repo`#1) and `prior_work.md`. This page says *what to test and where it shows*, never what a result must be. Every claim below has a "refuted if" line; a result that triggers it changes the claim, and I take it to `idea-repo` (see "When results do not carry it").

## 1. The story in one paragraph
Regression-adjustment estimators of the global average treatment effect (GATE) under network interference (Chin 2019; Han–Ugander 2023) fit outcome on functions of the assignment (own treatment, treated-neighbour fraction, …) and predict at all-treated and all-control. Published work shows they *can* work but gives no account of *how well, why, and when not*. We treat the estimator as **extrapolation from the observed exposure distribution to the two global corners** and ask what that predicts. The error splits into a **variance part** (OLS leverage of the corner contrast, scaling like d/(p(1−p)n)) and a **bias part** (curvature of the response × raw distance of the corner from the observed exposure support, roughly *not* growing with degree). The two parts have different drivers and, for the fraction feature, are predicted to move in opposite directions with degree (count, 2-hop and threshold mechanisms have their own predicted scalings), so "error grows with degree" is predicted to hold only where noise dominates. Abstract wording follows §3b: the bias part is *not* independent of d for (b) and (d). We test these scalings across interference mechanisms, graph families (synthetic and two real Facebook graphs), treatment probabilities and designs (Bernoulli, graph-cluster); map where regression beats and loses to difference-in-means (DM) and to exposure-mapping HT/Hájek; ask whether flexible/data-adaptive learners help; and test a data-computable two-part diagnostic against pre-registered trivial predictors. Not a new estimator: a verified, predictive account of when to trust an existing one. Positive, negative and mixed outcomes are all reported.

## 2. Position against prior work (Related work, one paragraph per cluster)
- *Regression GATE estimators*: Chin 2019 (estimator; Fig. 2 already shows the exposure-distribution mismatch qualitatively and draws the off-policy analogy), Han–Ugander 2023 (covariate generation/selection, block bootstrap). **We do not claim the extrapolation viewpoint as new**; we claim the quantified decomposition, its tests across mechanisms/graphs/designs, the regime map including where regression loses, and the diagnostic. Wording "to our knowledge within the literature checked".
- *Design-based exposure-mapping estimators*: Aronow–Samii 2017, Eckles et al. 2017, Ugander et al. 2013 (baselines and designs); Gao–Ding 2023 (regression for exposure-mapping estimands under overlap — different estimand; read in detail before the text states the difference); Thiyageswaran et al. 2024 (data-adaptive exposure; a simplified variant is run and named as such) and Shirani–Bayati 2024 (message passing for panel outcomes: related work only, not compared, since the study has one outcome per unit; the text says so in one sentence).
- *Misspecification / unknown interference*: Sävje et al. 2021, Leung 2022, Sävje 2023, Yu et al. 2022 — our setting is estimand = GATE with a possibly wrong response model.
- *Designs*: Karrer et al. 2021, Cortez et al. 2022 (optional), Chen et al. 2023, Leung 2022 rate. *Overlap/positivity*: Crump 2009, D'Amour 2021 (where the extrapolation analogy comes from).

shown.message:
I pushed Outline rev 7, which applies all seven items from the `idea-review-repo` review (`story-repo`#5), and closed #5. None of the changes narrows the paper.

- **C6:**
  - The verdict is worded "no evidence of a useful score", not "evidence of none". The intervals [−0.28, 0.34] and [−0.27, 0.22] fit both a useful and a useless score.
  - Absolute held-out R² of log|bias| now sits beside every gain. The exact-theory prediction scores 0.987 and is labelled a ceiling that uses the true response. Every data-computable predictor scores below a constant-only predictor.
  - Main-text Table 2 gains a constant-only row and an absolute-R² column.
  - The identifiability reading is labelled as interpretation.
  - The Han–Ugander-style CV loss scores −0.17 on the 84 Tier A cells, while the degree benchmarks score +0.31 and +0.33 there. I kept that detail in.
- **C1:** the d-exponent of 0.55 is compared with the exponent of the realised leverage, not with ½. The text says the CIs are MC-only and treat the 42 cells as independent.
- **C2:** mechanism (e), where 58% of cells fall inside the MC interval, gets its own sentence next to the pooled 82%.
- **C4:**
  - At d=5 the break-even s* is a bound (≤ 0.1), not an estimate.
  - Rule B is compared with the constant "always regression" rule (0.80). The 0.80 is this cell list's base rate, not a population frequency.
  - Rule A is a consistency check only.
- **C5:** the claim is two detected resolutions plus the planted partition. γ=0.3 gives one cluster on every synthetic graph.
- **Tier A:** the "flexible learners do not help" claim is scoped to this cell sample and these tunings.

I checked `bias_reference.csv`, `cv_benchmark.csv`, `c4_rule.csv`, `c1_exponents.csv` and `c6_verdict.csv` against the review's figures and they match.

I sent follow-ups to two roles. `analysis` (`experiment-repo`#6) is asked to predict s* from the C1 formula on existing cells, to add a CI for rule B against the constant rule, to give the realised-L exponent, and to add the constant-only row. `presentation` (`figtab-repo`#3) is told that Fig 6 shows two detected resolutions plus planted, that Fig 1 marks d=5 as a bound, and that Fig 7 and Table 2 show the constant line and absolute R².

`experiment-repo`#6, `idea-repo`#7 and `figtab-repo`#3 are still unanswered. `story-repo`#2 stays open.
